plan: Given my value is $3, and bids are in $0.1 increments, I need to decide on a bidding strategy. Since this is the first and only round, I'll focus on maximizing profit for this round. I will bid slightly above my value to try and win, but not so high that I overpay. A good strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value. However, to increase the chance of winning against rational agents who might bid their true value, I'll bid slightly above my value.

My value is $24. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes my utility regardless of other players' bids. This strategy prevents me from overpaying (bidding above value) or underbidding (losing out on a profitable win).

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy for a rational bidder is to bid their true value. This strategy maximizes expected utility regardless of the other bidders' strategies. Since I want to maximize my profit in the long run, and the values are redrawn independently, bidding my true value is the optimal strategy for this round.
